title: CamPU: A Multi-Camera Processing Unit for Deep Learning-based 3D Spatial Computing Systems
problem: Multi-camera systems require massive memory accesses that scale with the number of cameras, while DNN batch processing offers independent throughput improvements. This performance gap between image projection and DNN processing limits overall 3D spatial computing system performance.
motivation: 3D spatial computing systems understanding environments through multi-camera captures and deep learning are emerging, requiring efficient processing to enable real-time interaction with real-world objects.
method: CamPU reduces memory traffic during image projection by reusing data from overlapping camera views and within individual images. It uses an out-of-order image projection unit (which processes images in an optimized order rather than strictly sequentially) with local cache memory to eliminate redundant memory reads and hide delays from accessing main memory. A specialized blending unit efficiently handles the overlapping regions where adjacent cameras' views meet. The design was validated through RTL-level circuit simulation and tested with a deep neural network processing platform.
key_novelty: The core innovation is combining out-of-order image projection with local cache memory and overlap-aware blending to reduce memory traffic in multi-camera processing hardware.
contributions: Inter- and intra-data reuse methods for multi-camera images to minimize memory accesses
Out-of-order image projection unit with cache memory to increase throughput and hide latency
Overlap-aware blending unit for efficient handling of overlapping regions between cameras
RTL-validated CamPU-integrated DNN platform achieving 2.9x speedup over GPU
limitations: Not discussed in the abstract; power consumption, area overhead, scalability to different DNN architectures, and real-time latency requirements are not addressed.
primary_theme: Hardware acceleration for multi-camera 3D spatial computing
